hook: a huge dark cavity had hollowed out the jaw and the patient had never felt a thing
whatYouSee: A large dark scalloped cavity has hollowed out one side of the lower jaw and shoved a tooth out of place.
whyItMatters: It creeps along the length of the jaw rather than ballooning outward so it grows very large before anyone notices and it comes back after simple removal.
treatment: The lining is removed completely and the surrounding bone is treated and long term follow up is needed because it recurs.
takeaway: A big scalloped cavity running along the jaw with a displaced tooth is an odontogenic keratocyst.
